title: Beyond Refusals: AQI as an Intrinsic Alignment Diagnostic via Latent Geometry, Cluster Divergence, and Layer wise Pooled Representations
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the model's intrinsic latent alignment and its ability to geometrically separate safe representations from unsafe representations. In the context of religion, it specifically measured model responses and latent activations when presented with 'Religious Intolerance' prompts (e.g., mocking specific deities, making stereotypic claims, or generating hate speech against various faith groups).
findings: While the paper's primary finding is that the Alignment Quality Index (AQI) successfully detects latent representational collapse before surface-level alignment failures occur, it utilized prompts targeting religious intolerance to trigger these failures. The study showed that smaller models (e.g., TinyLLaMA, Phi-2) struggled to maintain latent boundary separation and easily fell into unsafe representational spaces when faced with adversarial variations of these religious intolerance prompts, even if their surface completions appeared compliant.
